hrZones.metaTitle: Heart rate zone calculator (%HRmax, Karvonen, LTHR) | Peakr
hrZones.metaDescription: Calculate your five heart rate training zones with the %HRmax, Karvonen (heart rate reserve) or LTHR method. Free, no account needed.
hrZones.title: Heart rate zones
hrZones.description: Your five training zones from max, resting or threshold heart rate.
hrZones.lead: Calculate your five training zones with the method that fits what you know about your heart rate.

methodInfo.percentMax: Zones as a percentage of your maximum heart rate. Simple and a good start.
methodInfo.karvonen: Uses your heart rate reserve (max minus resting). More personal, because it reflects your fitness.
methodInfo.lthr: Zones from your lactate threshold heart rate (Joe Friel). The most precise if you know your threshold.

hrZones.autoMethod: Chosen automatically: Karvonen as soon as you enter your resting heart rate.
hrZones.hrMaxEstimateNote: Estimated from your age (208 − 0.7 × age). A measured value makes your zones more accurate.

seo.heading: What are heart rate zones?
seo.body: Heart rate zones split your effort into five ranges, from very easy recovery (Zone 1) to all-out efforts (Zone 5). Training in the right zone makes sure easy days stay easy and hard days are hard enough to make you faster.

seo.heading: Which method should I use?
seo.body: %HRmax only needs your maximum heart rate (or your age for an estimate). Karvonen also uses your resting heart rate, so the zones reflect your fitness. LTHR, based on your lactate threshold heart rate from a 30-minute time trial, is the most precise for trained athletes.

seo.heading: How accurate is the age formula?
seo.body: The formula 208 − 0.7 × age is a population average – your real maximum can be 10–15 beats higher or lower. If you have seen a higher value at the end of an all-out effort, enter it as your max heart rate.

zone2.metaDescription: Find your Zone 2 heart rate range for easy aerobic training – with or without resting heart rate. Free, no account needed.
zone2.title: Zone 2 calculator
zone2.description: Find your easy aerobic range – and why it matters.
zone2.lead: Find the heart rate range for easy aerobic training – the foundation of every endurance plan.

benefits.base: Builds your aerobic base: more mitochondria and capillaries, so you get faster at the same heart rate.
benefits.fat: Trains your body to burn fat efficiently, which saves carbohydrates for hard efforts.
benefits.recovery: Easy enough to recover from quickly, so you can train more often without getting injured.
benefits.volume: Most endurance athletes do around 80 % of their training at this easy intensity.

zone2.restingHint: With resting heart rate the Karvonen method is used – more personal.

methodNote.percentMax: 60–70 % of your max heart rate ({{hrMax}} bpm).
methodNote.karvonen: 60–70 % of your heart rate reserve (Karvonen, max {{hrMax}} bpm).
methodNote.lthr: Based on your threshold heart rate.

zone2.talkTest: Check: you can still talk in full sentences. If not, slow down.

seo.heading: What is Zone 2 training?
seo.body: Zone 2 is the easy, conversational intensity where your body mainly uses fat for fuel. It feels almost too easy – and that is the point: you can do a lot of it and still recover for your harder sessions.

seo.heading: Why does my Zone 2 pace feel so slow?
seo.body: When you start training by heart rate, Zone 2 often means slowing down a lot, especially on hills or in the heat. After a few weeks of consistent easy training your pace at the same heart rate gets faster – that is your aerobic base improving.

pace.metaTitle: Running pace calculator & race time predictor | Peakr
pace.metaDescription: Predict your 5 km, 10 km, half marathon and marathon times and get your training pace zones from one recent race. Free, no account needed.
pace.title: Pace & race predictor
pace.description: Training paces and predicted race times from a recent race.
pace.lead: Get your training pace zones and predicted race times from one recent result.
pace.intro: Enter a recent race or all-out time trial. The more recent, the better.
pace.thresholdNote: About the pace you could hold for one hour.
pace.predictionsNote: Riegel formula. Assumes you train for the distance – longer races, especially the marathon, are often slower than predicted.

seo.heading: How are race times predicted?
seo.body: The calculator uses the Riegel formula, which scales a known race time to another distance with a fatigue factor. It works best between similar distances and assumes you have trained for the longer race.

seo.heading: What are pace zones for?
seo.body: Pace zones translate your current fitness into concrete training paces – from easy runs to threshold and interval sessions. On hilly routes or hot days, heart rate is the better guide for easy runs.

swim.metaTitle: Swim CSS calculator – Critical Swim Speed & pace zones | Peakr
swim.metaDescription: Calculate your Critical Swim Speed (CSS) and swim pace zones per 100 m from a 400 m and 200 m time trial. Free, no account needed.
swim.title: Swim pace (CSS)
swim.description: Critical Swim Speed and swim zones per 100 m from a simple test.
swim.lead: Calculate your Critical Swim Speed and swim pace zones per 100 m from two time trials.
swim.guideTitle: How to do the CSS test

guide.warmUp: Warm up for 10–15 minutes with easy swimming and a few short pick-ups.
guide.swim400: Swim 400 m as fast as you can at an even pace. Note the time.
guide.recover: Recover for 5–10 minutes with very easy swimming.
guide.swim200: Swim 200 m all-out. Note the time.
guide.record: Use the same pool and push-off starts for both efforts, then enter both times below.

swim.cssNote: Roughly the pace you can sustain for about 30 minutes.

seo.heading: What is Critical Swim Speed?
seo.body: CSS is the fastest pace you can hold for a long time without tiring rapidly – similar to the threshold pace in running. It is calculated from the difference between your 400 m and 200 m times.

seo.heading: Why pace instead of heart rate in the pool?
seo.body: Heart rate reads about 10–15 beats lower in water and wrist sensors are unreliable while swimming. Pace per 100 m from your CSS is a much more dependable target for swim sets.

privacy.metaDescription: How Peakr handles your personal data on this website and in the app.
privacy.title: Privacy policy

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This policy explains which personal data the Peakr website and the Peakr app process and why. It follows the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP) and, where applicable, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

sections.heading: Waitlist
sections.body: If you join the waitlist we store your email address, the consent text you agreed to and the time of your sign-up. We use this only to email you about the launch of Peakr. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). You can withdraw your consent at any time by emailing us; we will then delete your address. We delete the waitlist at the latest 12 months after launch.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: To use the app you create an account with your email address (sign-in link by email) or with Google or Apple; from Google or Apple we receive your email address and, if you allow it, your name. Accounts are managed with Supabase Auth. The legal basis is the performance of our contract with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

sections.heading: Training plan and sync
sections.body: The app stores your quiz answers, profile (such as age, heart rate values and availability), training zones, plan and workout history on your device. When you are signed in, this data is synchronised with our database so it is backed up and available on your other devices. We use it only to create and adapt your plan.

sections.heading: Route library
sections.body: Your route library contains the routes you import as GPX files (for example shared from Komoot), routes you planned in Strava and routes the app recognises from your own past activities. For each route we store its name, sport, start point, track, distance and elevation profile. The library is kept on your device and, when you are signed in, synchronised with our database as a backup and for your other devices. We use it only to suggest routes for your own sessions and to evaluate them; it is never shown to other users. You can delete single routes in the app; all routes are deleted together with your account.

sections.heading: Strava
sections.body: If you connect Strava, we receive an access token, the activities you record (for example sport, start time, duration, distance, elevation, heart rate and route) and the routes you planned in Strava. For outdoor runs and rides we also store the recorded activity streams – distance, altitude, time, heart rate and GPS track, reduced to about one point every 25 metres – to evaluate your sessions against the terrain. When you connect, we import up to 180 days of your past activities so the app can recognise the routes you run and ride regularly. When you create or recalibrate your plan, you can also let us read your runs, rides and swims of the last 60 days and the heart-rate zones you set in Strava; you see the list and choose which activities to use. These are stored separately as reference data only: they calibrate the starting point of your plan (for example weekly volume, easy pace and heart-rate zones), and they are never added to your training history, never counted as completed sessions and never shown in your progress. This reference data is deleted when you disconnect Strava or delete your account. We use this data only to adapt your own plan, build your own route library and mark sessions as done. It is never shown to other users and never used to train artificial intelligence or machine learning models (as required by the Strava API Agreement). You can disconnect Strava at any time in the app or in your Strava settings; we then delete the token, the imported activities, activity streams and Strava routes and stop importing. Routes you already have in your route library stay there until you delete them or your account.

sections.heading: Maps (MapTiler)
sections.body: When the app shows a route map, it loads map tiles from MapTiler AG (api.maptiler.com, Switzerland). For this, your device's IP address and the map area being displayed are sent to MapTiler; we do not send them your account or other personal data. MapTiler uses this data only to deliver the map. The maps are based on OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed under the Open Database License, ODbL). The legal basis is our legitimate interest in showing routes on a map (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

sections.heading: Push notifications
sections.body: If you allow notifications, we store a push token for your device to send your daily workout reminder and the trial reminder. Notifications are delivered through Expo and Google Firebase Cloud Messaging or the Apple Push Notification service. You can turn them off in the app or in your device settings; the token is deleted together with your account.

sections.heading: Payments (planned)
sections.body: Subscriptions are not available yet. Once they are, payments in the app are processed by Google Play or the App Store and payments on this website by Stripe Payments Europe Ltd.; we never see your full card details. RevenueCat Inc. manages which subscription your account has, across app and website. [TODO: complete this section before payments launch.]

sections.heading: Database hosting (Supabase)
sections.body: Waitlist sign-ups, accounts and synchronised app data are stored with Supabase Inc. as our processor in a data centre in the EU [TODO: confirm region]. Supabase processes the data only on our behalf, under a data processing agreement.

sections.heading: Website hosting (Vercel)
sections.body: This website is hosted by Vercel Inc. When you visit it, Vercel processes technical data such as your IP address, browser type and the requested page to deliver the site and protect it against abuse. These logs are kept only briefly. Data may be transferred to the USA based on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses.

sections.heading: Free calculators
sections.body: The calculators run in your browser. The values you enter are not sent to us or stored.

sections.heading: Cookies and analytics
sections.body: This website currently uses no tracking cookies and no analytics. Fonts are served from our own domain, not from third parties. If we add analytics later, it will only load after you have given your consent, and this policy will be updated first.

sections.heading: Retention and deletion
sections.body: We keep your data as long as you have an account. You can delete your account at any time in the app (Profile → Account) or by email – see “Delete account” for details. Payment records are kept as long as Swiss law requires.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask for access to, correction or deletion of your data, restrict or object to its processing, and receive it in a portable format. You can also lodge a complaint with a data protection authority – in Switzerland the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).

terms.metaDescription: Terms of service for the Peakr app and website: subscription, free trial, renewal, cancellation and withdrawal.
terms.title: Terms of service

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: These terms apply to the Peakr app and the website (together “Peakr”), offered by the provider named above. By creating an account or starting a subscription you accept these terms.

sections.heading: The service
sections.body: Peakr creates personal training plans and, as an add-on, nutrition and body tracking. The plans and calculations are general training guidance, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting a training programme if you have health concerns, and stop training if you feel unwell.

sections.heading: Account
sections.body: You must be at least [TODO: minimum age, e.g. 16] years old to create an account; the weight-loss goal is only available from 18. Keep your login secure – you are responsible for activity on your account.

sections.heading: Subscription and prices
sections.body: The full plan requires a paid subscription, billed monthly or yearly. The current prices are shown on the pricing page and before you confirm a purchase, including any taxes. App purchases are processed by Google Play or the App Store under their terms; website purchases by Stripe.

sections.heading: 7-day free trial
sections.body: New subscribers get a 7-day free trial, once per account. You enter your payment details when you start the trial; nothing is charged during the trial and the exact date of the first charge is shown before you confirm. We remind you one day before the trial ends. If you cancel before the trial ends, you pay nothing.

sections.heading: Automatic renewal
sections.body: After the trial, the subscription starts and renews automatically for the same period (month or year) at the then-current price until you cancel. We will tell you in advance about any price change, and you can cancel before it applies.

sections.heading: Cancellation
sections.body: You can cancel at any time with effect from the end of the current billing period. App subscriptions are cancelled in Google Play or the App Store, website subscriptions in the Stripe customer portal. You keep access until the end of the paid period; afterwards your account and history remain and your plan becomes read-only. Deleting your account does not cancel a subscription.

sections.heading: Right of withdrawal
sections.body: If you are a consumer in the EU, you have a 14-day right of withdrawal for website purchases. Because the free trial lets you test Peakr first, you agree that the service starts immediately and acknowledge that [TODO: have the wording of the withdrawal clause and waiver legally reviewed]. For app purchases, the refund rules of Google Play and the App Store apply. Swiss law does not provide a general right of withdrawal for online purchases.

sections.heading: Your content and third-party services
sections.body: Data you enter or import (for example from Strava) remains yours; we use it only to provide Peakr to you, as described in the privacy policy. Connected services such as Strava are governed by their own terms.

sections.heading: Availability and changes
sections.body: We work to keep Peakr available but cannot guarantee uninterrupted operation. We may develop the service further. We may change these terms for good reason; we will inform you in advance, and if you do not agree you can cancel before the changes take effect.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: We are liable without limitation for intent and gross negligence. Otherwise our liability is excluded to the extent permitted by law. [TODO: have the liability clause legally reviewed.]

sections.heading: Applicable law and jurisdiction
sections.body: Swiss law applies, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Place of jurisdiction is [TODO: city of the registered address], Switzerland. Mandatory consumer protection rules of your country of residence remain unaffected.

features.metaTitle: Features – hybrid plans, heart rate zones, terrain & real life | Peakr
features.metaDescription: One plan for running, cycling, swimming and strength: heart rate zones first, terrain-aware sessions, commutes, travel, winter sports and weather – synced with Strava.
features.title: Everything your training needs, in one plan
features.lead: Peakr combines your sports into one plan, prescribes it in heart rate zones, knows your terrain and adapts when real life happens.

hybrid.title: One hybrid plan
hybrid.body: Pick any combination of running, cycling and swimming – from your first 5 km to a full-distance triathlon – and add strength at home or in the gym.
points: One training-load budget for all sports: a hard Saturday ride makes Sunday’s run easier automatically.
Strength is periodised with your endurance phases – no heavy legs before a key session or your long day.
Base, build, peak and taper phases, with a recovery week every three to four weeks.
Brick sessions (bike → run) for triathlon and duathlon goals.

heartRate.title: Heart rate zones first
heartRate.body: Every session is prescribed in heart rate zones, with a strong focus on Zone 2. Pace and power are hints, not the goal.
points: Zones from %HRmax, Karvonen or your lactate threshold – calculated during onboarding.
About 80 % easy and 20 % hard, so easy days stay easy.
Swimming uses pace per 100 m from your Critical Swim Speed, because heart rate is unreliable in the water.
View and edit your zones at any time – the plan recalculates.

terrain.title: Terrain intelligence
terrain.body: Peakr knows how hilly each run and ride is and plans around your gradient instead of ignoring it.
points: Pick a route for today’s session from your own routes or routes recognised from your Strava activities.
Duration and pace targets per kilometre, adjusted to the gradient.
Grade-adjusted evaluation after each run, so hilly days compare fairly with flat ones.
Export the route and the structured workout to your watch.

realLife.title: Calendar & real life
realLife.body: Your plan lives in an editable calendar and adapts to the week you actually have.
points: Move a session and the week rebalances – with a warning if two hard days end up back to back.
Bike or run commutes count as easy training and are planned first.
Travel mode and irregular weeks: rebuild a week in seconds.
Cross-country skiing, ski touring and snowshoeing count as real training in winter.
Rain, snow or ice? Get an indoor alternative with the same training effect.

Smoothed weight trend instead of daily scale noise.
Safe targets: never below your basal needs, at most 1 % of body weight per week.

items.question: Is there a free version?
items.answer: The calculators on this website are free. In the app, the quiz, your forecast and a preview of week 1 are free – the full plan needs a subscription or a running trial.

items.question: Do I need the Gym add-on for strength training?
items.answer: No. Your plan includes strength sessions and you can mark them done with duration and effort. The Gym add-on adds set-by-set logging, history, statistics and sharing to Strava. It is a separate subscription with its own 7-day free trial.
